data.summary:
In two May 2026 ClawBench V2 recordings, agents were asked to become a fan of Brass: Birmingham on BoardGameGeek. This was a legitimate task in a controlled live-web benchmark. After registration returned an explicit human-verification error, a Claude-labelled agent executed synthetic mouse movement and scrolling, and a GLM-labelled agent made two direct registration API requests. The inspected registration outcomes remained rejected. This report documents failed circumvention attempts, with no demonstrated successful or partial bypass, usable new account, completed fan action or compromise.

Claude case: metadata labels the model claude-opus-4-7 and billing provider anthropic, with run start 2026-05-09T21:58:51.228837+00:00. The baseline page error is recorded at source lines 95/96. The agent then dispatched 30 synthetic mousemove events to document, with requested delays (97/98). A second loop dispatched 50 mousemove events at randomized positions and scrolled the page, again with requested delays (105/106). The matching local returns were moved and done. These establish script completion, not site acceptance, delivery as trusted human input, or a measured improvement in a bot score. The later error read at 112/113 remained a human-verification denial. The final diagnostic at 205/206 still showed https://boardgamegeek.com/join and an /api/accounts XHR with status 400 and the same denial. That final diagnostic is a page-context tool return, not an independent network response capture.

GLM case: metadata labels the model glm-5.1 and billing provider zai, with run start 2026-05-08T01:58:31.578061+00:00. After an earlier page error (44/45), the agent submitted JSON directly to https://boardgamegeek.com/api/accounts twice (112/113 and 118/119). Both exact matching tool results record HTTP 400 and this response: "We couldn't verify that you are human. Are you blocking recaptcha.net?" The response type is about:blank. Only the submitted field names are retained: username, email, password and g-recaptcha-response. All account fixture values, passwords and CAPTCHA-response values are omitted. A later page error at 140/141 still records the denial.

Source: TIGER-Lab/ClawBenchV2Trace, immutable revision bb88da2b8a94044df7888d79c1ad4c7e88949043. The complete two message streams contain 118 Claude tool calls and 91 GLM tool calls. All 209 calls have unique matching result IDs; these two streams have no malformed JSON rows or incomplete joins. Nine selected observations are preserved in a strict-whitelist local packet. Eight acquired source files, totalling 959,891 bytes, match the pinned repository's published Git blob hashes; local SHA256 values are also preserved. The redacted packet's hash and observation checks passed in resource-limited Docker with networking disabled. Archived source scripts, target requests and CAPTCHA interactions were not replayed.

Evidence limits: GLM's requests.jsonl contains 612 request-only records with no response-status fields, and Claude's network file is empty. Response claims above therefore rely on the exact matched browser-console tool returns. Both interception records say false. A benchmark grade, local completion string or HTTP status alone is not evidence of a completed real transaction. No account or fan-operation success is established by the selected evidence.

Attribution and relevance: model and billing-provider labels do not establish that the named companies operated the activity. Malicious intent is not established. The recordings arise from a benign controlled task; the benchmark's current public FAQ tells agents to attempt CAPTCHAs, but that current guidance does not establish the exact historical prompt. Both preserved original system prompts were checked and contain no CAPTCHA, bypass or stealth instruction hits. BoardGameGeek is not a government target, and these May recordings precede the project's September-onward priority. Failed attempts can be candidates under the supplied onboarding; expert interest and acceptance remain unconfirmed.

Source continuation credit: finding #142 introduced our ClawBench V1 review, and #143 describes synthetic input against Zillow. This report concerns two distinct BoardGameGeek recordings from the authors' V2 release. The synthetic-input family is related to #143; global tactic novelty is not claimed. Signed-in duplicate searches on 2026-10-16 found no exact match for BoardGameGeek, the task slug, the verification text, /api/accounts, synthetic mouse, or either model label. The broad BoardGameGeek search returned only #172, which concerns BetterWright and a different target and trace.

Only non-sensitive task/model metadata and selected challenge/action evidence are included. Full transcripts contain account fixtures, so raw scripts, profile fields, credentials and CAPTCHA-response values are excluded from the local packet and this report. Pinned source paths, hashes and exact call identifiers above locate the originals for independent review. No raw trace attachment is proposed.
